newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher but downtrend intact.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher but downtrend intact.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher for a second day Wednesday, but the month long downtrend is not seen broken yet, analysts said.
"The market has flushed out some weak shorts, but there's still probably more reasons to sell than to buy," Mitsui USA Co bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
"Producers have bought back some hedges this year and are probably a bit uncomfortable about their exposure now, so any bounce will probably be met by hedger selling," he said.
COMEX December gold ended up $1.30 an ounce at $382.30, after trading in a $380.60-383.30 range.
In bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted around $379.70, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $380.30, and the New York close Tuesday around $378.60.
While sentiment remained bearish, analysts noted gold has bounced from the $370-380 level several times in the past three and a half years.
COMEX December silver ended up 1.7 cents at $4.927 an ounce, after trading in a $4.900-4.980 range.
The spot gold/silver ratio declined in the past week, and ended at 77.33, down from an 18 month high of 78.55 on September 20.

"Based on the closing price for the third quarter and implied volatility levels for the latest quarter, the implied price range for gold to one standard deviation is $369.79 to $391.21," MCM analyst Peter McTeague said.
"This is the most likely range for the fourth quarter based on what options traders are pricing into option premiums," he added.

While gold has been in a persistent downtrend in the past month, options volatilities have been close to record lows, but this may be more the result of the high open interest in gold options of over 300,000 COMEX contracts, analysts said.

But investor demand for precious metals is still seen limited by low inflation, and a strong equity market, while industrial and investor demand in other countries has been restrained by a strong U.S. dollar pushing up the cost of precious metals in local currencies, analysts said.
Technically, on the daily charts, momentum indicators have been showing some divergence from recent price downtrends, analysts noted.

But popular moving average indicators, such as the four, nine and 18 day triple moving-average trend following indicator, has not yet shown much sign of a turnaround for any of the four metals in the NYMEX/COMEX precious metals complex, analysts said.
NYMEX October platinum ended $1.00 at $386.00 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium closed up $1.85 at $122.40 an ounce.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
